name: Earth science: predicting recent global warming from forcing and early observations
description: Fit a model of annual global mean surface temperature on the 1850-1979 HadCRUT5 record, given radiative forcing histories and an ENSO index for 1750-2024, and predict the 1980-2024 anomalies without seeing any later temperature. The score is the root-mean-square error of the predicted anomalies.

sources.locator: Lean and Rind (2008): multiple regression of observed global and regional temperature on anthropogenic, volcanic, solar and ENSO influences.
Haustein et al. (2017): a simple impulse-response climate model fitted to observed temperature and forcing to attribute warming (Global Warming Index).
Otto et al. (2013): energy-budget estimates of transient and equilibrium climate response from observed warming and forcing.
Morice et al. (2021): HadCRUT5, the global temperature analysis whose annual means and 95% ranges are the target.
Forster et al. (2025): Indicators of Global Climate Change 2024, the effective radiative forcing time series 1750-2024 used as inputs.
HadCRUT5.0.2.0 global annual summary series (Open Government Licence; retrieved 2026-10-10); 1850-2024 used.
Best-estimate ERF aggregates 1750-2024 (output/ERF_best_aggregates_1750-2024.csv, MIT licence) at a pinned commit.

requirements.datasets: Derived from pinned public sources by python3 scripts/prepare_earth.py (hashes in catalog/earth-data-lock.json).

evaluation.benchmark: Earth science: predicting recent global warming from forcing and early observations
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: predict_gmst(training, inputs) -> float array (45,) of annual global mean near-surface temperature anomalies (deg C from 1961-1990, HadCRUT5 analysis) for 1980-2024. training holds year (1850-1979), gmst and its 95% range gmst_low, gmst_high. inputs holds forcing_year (1750-2024) and forcing, a dict of annual effective radiative forcing series (W m-2, Forster et al. 2025 update of IPCC AR6) for CO2, CH4, N2O, halogen, minor, O3, H2O_stratospheric, contrails, aerosol-radiation_interactions, aerosol-cloud_interactions, BC_on_snow, land_use, solar, volcanic, anthro and total; enso_year, enso_month and relative_nino34 (1854-01 to 2024-12: ERSSTv5 Nino 3.4 anomaly minus the 20S-20N mean SST anomaly, from 1951-1980 monthly climatologies); and predict_years (1980-2024). No temperature after 1979 is provided. The candidate runs in a separate sandboxed process (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and pandas importable; no file, network or subprocess access; one thread) with 60 s of CPU time for fitting and all predictions together; seed any randomness so that results are deterministic. Score: root-mean-square error (deg C) of the 45 predicted anomalies against HadCRUT5; lower is better. Wrong shapes, NaN or values outside [-5, 5] deg C are invalid

limitations: The forcing inputs are not independent of the target: the assessed aerosol forcing behind the AR6 and 2024 updates uses observational constraints that include the recent warming, so the held-out period leaks partly into the inputs.

Recent global temperatures are widely known; a candidate can encode remembered values or trends instead of inferring them from 1850-1979, so the score measures emulation skill only for candidates restricted to the training data. Freeze a candidate and test it on later years before any claim.

Only 45 annual values are scored and internal variability not explained by the ENSO index (roughly 0.1 deg C per year) limits the attainable error; HadCRUT5 itself has a 95% range of about 0.03-0.05 deg C in this period.
A better score is a better statistical or physical emulator of observed warming given these forcings, not by itself a new estimate of climate sensitivity.
HadCRUT5 is a live product; if past annual means are revised, the derived-file hash check fails and the data must be re-recorded.

The candidate runs in a sandboxed child process that never receives temperatures after 1979, and no statement of the candidate is executed in the evaluator's process; outside macOS (kernel sandbox) deliberately hostile native code could bypass the file policy.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value exists for this split. Internal references fitted on 1850-1979: linear regression on total forcing (the seed) 0.464 deg C, a two-layer energy-balance model with illustrative, uncalibrated parameters (lambda 1.3, gamma 0.7 W m-2 K-1; heat capacities 8 and 100 W yr m-2 K-1) plus a fitted offset 0.163 deg C, and a Lean-Rind-style regression on smoothed anthropogenic, volcanic and solar forcing and ENSO 0.750 deg C.

sources.title: How natural and anthropogenic influences alter global and regional surface temperatures: 1889 to 2006

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Explain and predict observed global mean temperature change from radiative forcing and internal variability (attribution and transient climate response).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: How much warming follows a given forcing (the transient climate response) is one of the most consequential numbers in climate science; simple models fitted to observed warming and forcing are the standard tools for attribution and for constraining it.

papers.title: How natural and anthropogenic influences alter global and regional surface temperatures: 1889 to 2006
papers.primary_goal: Quantify the contributions of anthropogenic, volcanic, solar and ENSO influences to observed temperature changes.
papers.task_relation: The task scores the same kind of forcing-plus-ENSO model of observed global temperature, but asks it to predict a held-out later period.

papers.title: A real-time Global Warming Index
papers.primary_goal: Attribute observed global warming to human and natural forcing in real time with a simple climate response model fitted to observations.
papers.task_relation: Candidates can be such response models; the task verifies them on years withheld from fitting.

papers.title: Energy budget constraints on climate response
papers.primary_goal: Estimate transient and equilibrium climate response from observed warming, forcing and ocean heat uptake.
papers.task_relation: A model that predicts the held-out warming well must encode a realistic transient response.

science_relevance.reason: The cited papers' main goal is explaining observed temperature change from forcing (attribution and climate response), the problem the local task scores out of sample; no reproduction of their numbers is claimed.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Crossref metadata checked on 2026-10-10; licences of HadCRUT5 (OGL) and the forcing repository (MIT) checked; relative Nino 3.4 values checked against known El Nino and La Nina events; evaluator run on the pinned data.
